Name: objects_from_statements
Title: From Particle Cuts to Class Boundaries: An Exact Statement–Object Program for a Jet Tagger
Short Hypothesis: A jet tagger builds its class boundaries from objects made of statements: cuts on single particles; the particle sets passing each cut, read by count and summed momentum and position; neurons as statements on those objects; classes as combinations of neuron objects. High-level jet variables are built over the layers in order of algebraic depth. For JEDI-linear the chain can be written as formulas from the input to the logits.
Related Work: Rai & Ganguly 2605.09881 (ParT top-tagging circuit; residual stream aligned with energy correlators); Wang et al. 2412.03673 (ParT attention); Komiske, Metodiev & Thaler (EFN/PFN: sum-pooled per-particle filters); Faucett et al. 2010.11998 (mapping networks to EFPs); Dreyer, Salam & Soyez 1807.04758 (Lund plane); mechanistic interpretability circuits (Olah et al.; Conmy et al. ACDC; Geiger et al. causal abstraction).; Cammarata (Goodfire, 2026) 'Neural Networks Are Already Clean': units have one main job once tooling is right; superposition as last hypothesis.
Experiments: E2 particle cuts in physical units
E6 mass as products of moments
E7 neurons on the network's own objects + stage substitution
E10 high-level variables over layers vs algebraic depth
Risk Factors and Limitations: Fixed-point rounding perturbs the exact identities (3.8% of calls); JEDI-linear is not permutation invariant (reads slots in pT order); probes measure readability, not use, unless paired with causal edits; one dataset (hls4ml jets).
